name: Boerewors stew
summary: Chunks of browned boerewors simmered with potatoes and carrots in a rich tomato and onion gravy, a weeknight one-pot for pap or rice.
about: When the braai is rained out, many South African families cook their boerewors in the pot instead. Browned and simmered in a tomato and onion sauce with potatoes, it turns one coil of wors into a filling family meal.

ingredients.name: Potatoes
ingredients.note: medium, peeled and cut into chunks

steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Brown the boerewors pieces in two batches, turning them, for about 5 minutes a batch, until coloured all over. Lift them out onto a plate.
Turn the heat down to medium and fry the onions and green pepper in the fat left in the pot for 6–8 minutes, until soft and starting to brown.
Add the garlic, paprika, cumin and thyme and stir for 1 minute, until fragrant. Stir in the tomato paste and cook for 1 minute more, until it darkens slightly.
Add the chopped tomatoes, beef stock, potatoes, carrots and sugar and bring to the boil, scraping up the browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
Return the boerewors to the pot, cover and simmer over low heat for 25–30 minutes, stirring now and then, until a knife slides easily into the potatoes and carrots.

Take the lid off and simmer for 5–10 minutes more, until the gravy has thickened enough to coat the potatoes. Season with salt and pepper (the wors is already salty, so taste first), scatter with parsley and serve with pap or rice.
prepNote: Keeps 2 days in the fridge and reheats well; add a splash of water if the gravy has thickened.
